_readme: Per-model language support for live captions, keyed by the exact model
name typed into Settings -> Live captions (live_caption_{backend}_model).
Edit this file directly -- it's plain data, no deploy pipeline of its
own, but it IS bundled into the frontend build like everything else in
web/src, so a change needs `npm run build` (or a dev server reload) to
show up, same as editing recording.ts by hand would.
Two lists per model, and they can legitimately disagree:
confirmed  -- codes actually observed to work (or fail) against a
real running instance of THIS app. This is what the
language picker restricts itself to.
documented -- the wider set the underlying model's own vendor
docs/README claim support for. Kept alongside confirmed
as a worklist: if you test one of these against your own
deployment and it works, move it into confirmed by hand.
unbounded: true means the model is Whisper/VibeVoice-shaped (broad,
near-universal coverage, no fixed short list worth hardcoding) -- the
picker falls back to the generic LIVE_CAPTION_LANGUAGES list for these
and for any model name this file doesn't mention at all.
Sourced August 2026 from vendor docs, cited per model below -- not from
a controlled test of every code against every deployment. Treat
'documented' as 'plausible, per the vendor', not 'guaranteed to work here'.

nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b.note: NVIDIA's own model card and the parakeet.cpp README (the C++/ggml port this app's live-stt server is built on -- see ServerInfoResponse.parakeet_ref in asr.proto) both describe this as a 40-locale model with automatic language detection, no selection needed at runtime. That directly contradicts a real error seen against this app's own live-stt deployment (`parakeet: unknown target_lang 'zh'. Valid examples: en-US, en, en-GB, enGB, es-ES, esES, es-US, es, ...`), so 'confirmed' stays narrow -- English/Spanish only. Everything else NVIDIA documents is still offered in the picker, marked "(untested here)" -- pick one to actually try it (a failure now surfaces as an in-app warning instead of silence, see useLiveCaption's CaptionWarning), and move it into 'confirmed' below by hand once it's worked. It's also possible this deployment is actually running the separate English-only nvidia/nemotron-speech-streaming-en-0.6b checkpoint under this model name; if so, none of the untested ones will ever pass and confirmed is the real ceiling.

realtime_eou_120m-v1.note: nvidia/parakeet_realtime_eou_120m-v1 -- a 120M-parameter streaming model built specifically for low-latency end-of-utterance detection (see asr.proto's EndOfUtterance/Ready.supports_turn_detection, and live_caption.py's docstring on why nemotron above needs a periodic-flush fallback that this model doesn't). Its own model card documents English only, with no punctuation or capitalization either -- a separate limitation, not language-related.

lfm2.5-audio-1.5b-realtime.note: LiquidAI/LFM2.5-Audio-1.5B -- the realtime pipeline model this app's /v1/realtime backend defaults to. English only today; a separate -JP checkpoint adds Japanese (add "ja" to confirmed by hand if that's what's actually deployed here), and Liquid AI has said broader multilingual support matching LFM2.5-Base's own coverage is in progress but not shipped as of this writing.

whisper-large-turbo-q8_0.note: whisper-large-v3-turbo, ggml q8_0 quantization (whisper.cpp) -- Whisper's large models are multilingual across ~99 languages, so this app's own generic language list applies rather than a model-specific short list. One real caveat: the turbo distillation was never trained for the separate cross-language *translation* task (only same-language transcription), which doesn't affect the language picker itself.

vibevoice-cpp-asr.note: microsoft/VibeVoice-ASR -- this app's batch diarization_model default, not a live-caption backend, but documented here too since diarize.py and this file share the same "which models has anyone actually looked up" concern. 50+ languages, auto-detects, no language parameter needed at all.
